newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PCI says scouting for a local partner.
newsitem.headline: PCI says scouting for a local partner.

text.p: The Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCIBank) is scouting for a local bank for a possible merger to enable it to meet head-on fierce competition in the industry, its president said on Monday.
"We are looking around for a local partner," PCIBank president Rafael Buenaventura told reporters at the listing ceremony of the bank's financing unit at the Philippine Stock Exchange.
The unit, PCI Leasing and Finance Inc, made its debut at 7.60 pesos, up from its offer price of 6.95 pesos.
Buenaventura denied stockmarket rumours that PCIBank had preliminary negotiations for a merger with the Philippine Bank of communications (PBCom).
"That's just a rumour. It's too early to identify our likely partner. We are just starting to look around," he said.

Buenaventura said PCIBank needed to merge with a bank which can provide "synergy" to its present operations. "We want to strengthen some areas in our operations like consumer and the Chinese community market," he added.
The entry of foreign banks in the local banking industry has forced some existing players to merge to fortify their positions.
"We will see more mergers," Buenaventura said. Some 14 branches have been set up by foreign banks, excluding networks maintained by joint ventures between local and foreign banks.
The local banking industry is expected to be better this year, from the 1996 growth forecast of 30 percent, he said.
"And the economy is growing fast so banks have to meet the bigger requirements of their customers," Buenaventura said.
Last year, PCIBank was prevented by the Supreme Court to increase its authorised capital through a rights offering.

The restraining order was issued pending the resolution of a legal dispute over the ownership of the sequestered shares of the PCIBank, equivalent to 10 percent of the oustanding capital stock, said Buenaventura.
The Philippine's powerful Lopez family, which has interests in electricity generating and broadcasting, is seeking to recover the shares that were taken over by members of the Romualdez family.
Imelda Marcos, wife of late president Ferdinand Marcos, is a member of the Romualdez family.
The government sequestered the disputed shares after the Marcoses were overthrown in a popular revolt in 1986.

Buenaventura said PCIBank can "afford" not to increase its capital this year. "But eventually we have to increase our capital base to meet the increasing borrowing requirements of our customers," he said.
